title: Township for Godot 4 is live: NPC daily routines and 50 places drawn in code
html:
Township is live for Godot 4: give every NPC in your 2D town a day, and let the player see it happen. Homes, jobs, shops that open and shut, night shifts, market days and festivals, walked on your own TileMapLayer with doors that open. 50 places drawn in code wake when their people arrive.

What it does

  • A schedule is a list of stops with no end times, so a shift from 22:00 to 07:00 is the ordinary case. Second schedules take over on market days, weekdays, flags and story variables.
  • Where someone is depends only on the clock. A scene loaded at noon, a save and a time skip are simply right, with no tracking code, and someone in a scene you have not loaded still has a stop you can ask about.
  • The places respond: the forge's coals brighten when the smith arrives, an awning rolls out at opening time, a window lights after dark while someone is home, and the lamplighter's round lights the street lamps one by one.
  • The routine board draws everyone's whole day, a night shift as one band off the right edge and on at the left. Use it as your debugger or as the town's roster in your game.

Tested

  • Every place photographed under Forward+ and Compatibility: 100 frames, zero engine errors, all 50 distinct under each renderer.
  • The shipped zip installed into a blank Godot 4.7.2 project under both renderers: the Readme example as written, every schedule rule, walking checked to the pixel against the clock, doors, a way out to another scene, a conversation, saving through JSON, your own SpriteFrames, and every preset dropped in.
  • 6 attacks, including a path with spaces and non Latin characters, a third renderer, a renamed addon folder and a big town timed with vsync off; 414 Readme claims checked against the shipped files.
  • Eleven sabotages of the engine, each one required to turn the right check red. They found three of our own checks that could not fail, and those were rewritten.
  • Looking at a reel of the demo found the worst defect, past every green check: the lamps never lit. A schedule tighter than its walk meant the lamplighter never arrived anywhere, and jumped at every new stop. People now turn from wherever they had got to, still worked out from the clock alone, and the town names any stop that cannot be walked in its time.

Free lite

The page carries a free MIT lite: 12 of the 50 places and the schedule engine, with its own demo.

Where this line stands: 26 Godot listings live from this studio, 3 purchases so far (read from the store the day this went live).

Disclosure: the scripts, presets and demo were written with AI, and everything they draw is computed by that code; the cover is a generated illustration, and the demo's map tiles are from our own Verdant 09 Town, also AI generated.
